title: fix(automation): require the wait / boundary_event config block at the contract, retire the executor's silent timer default
body:
Fixes #17928

A `wait` flow node with no `waitEventConfig` block parsed clean and ran to `{ success: true, suspend: true }` — parked forever, reporting success, from the state a freshly created node is in. This PR makes the protocol refuse that document, makes the executor refuse it loudly when a stored one still reaches `execute`, and settles the two default-free optional keys the same ruling covers.

⚠️ **Takeover of an orphaned branch.** Five commits were already on `claude/issue-17928-wait-node-config-required` when this session picked it up; their author's session died before a PR existed. They were diffed and judged, not trusted, and their history was not rewritten — everything since is added on top.

## The ruling this implements

Maintainer, decision batch #127 item 5 (C′), recorded on objectui#9354, verbatim and untranslated:

> 「16678 具体解释，计划用哪个字段判断经理。其他同意」

C′ as presented: the protocol is the source of truth; a designer never invents a default the protocol does not apply; a default the protocol *should* have is declared by the protocol; **a required key has no "unset behaves as"**.

## What lands

**A — the contract stops accepting the silent shape (`packages/spec`)**

`FlowNodeSchema` now requires `waitEventConfig` on a `type: 'wait'` node and `boundaryConfig` on a `type: 'boundary_event'` node, and the inline `waitEventConfig` block in `flowNodeObject()` requires a non-blank `timerDuration` under `eventType: 'timer'`. There is no `WaitEventConfigSchema` export — the block is declared inline, and this body said otherwise until the review round. Each issue is raised under the block's own key, so a flow-level parse reports a **top-level** node at `nodes[i].waitEventConfig` with the remedy in the message.

⚠️ **Where the refusal bites, stated accurately.** A node nested in an ADR-0031 **region body** is refused at a different door, at a different time. `parseFlowNodeRegions` parses each region slot with `safeParse` and, on a refusal, leaves that region **raw** and continues — a policy that predates this change — so `FlowSchema.safeParse` of a flow whose `loop` body holds a block-less `wait` answers `true`. What refuses it is the **region contract** (`LoopConfigSchema` / `ParallelConfigSchema` / `TryCatchConfigSchema`) at `body.nodes[i].waitEventConfig`, which is the same contract the container node's executor parses its config through at execute time — so the nested shape still cannot run, it is refused one door later and by node id. Both halves are pinned in `flow.test.ts` ("nested in a region: the flow parse leaves it raw, and the REGION contract refuses it by path"), and the ADR-0087 entry's `acceptanceCriteria` has said so from the start.

⚠️ **The `timerDuration` requirement is BLOCK-scoped, not node-type-scoped.** It sits on the `waitEventConfig` block, so any node type carrying that key is held to it: `FlowNodeSchema.safeParse` of a `start` node spelled `waitEventConfig: { eventType: 'timer' }` answers `false` at this head and `true` on `main`, with both controls green (the same node with `timerDuration: 'PT1H'`, and a plain `start` with no block, both `true`). It only ever narrows, and the block is inert on node types no executor reads it from, so the practical reach is `wait` — but a stack that spells the key elsewhere must be edited too, which is why the changeset and the migration entry now say "scan for the KEY, not only for the node type".

⛔ The two required enums (`wait.eventType`, `boundary_event.eventType`) get **no** default: a required key has no "unset behaves as", and an indefinite park, if one is ever wanted, is its own declared `eventType`.

**B — the executor follows the contract (`packages/services/service-automation`)**

`wait-node.ts` carried `(node.waitEventConfig ?? {})` and `String(wec.eventType ?? 'timer')` under a comment declaring the second deliberate — "a wait node without one is a VALID TIMER WAIT". Both fallbacks are retired and the comment is deleted with the reversal named. A node that still reaches `execute` without the block (a stored pre-migration document on a path that skipped the parse) is now a **guard refusal** — `errorClass: 'guard'`, so a `fault` edge cannot route a metadata defect into a handler that reports success — and it **logs**, naming the node and the remedy, because the defect being closed was silence. Two corrections ride the same return: the timer branch stops answering `output` as a present key holding `undefined`, and it is absent when no deadline was computed.

`boundary_event` gets the contract half only: the runtime registers **no executor** for that type at all (`NO_EXECUTOR` plus a startup warn), so there is no silent executor branch behind it.

**C — the two optional keys, decided by reading the executors rather than the Zod**

| key | what the executor applies for an absent value | declared |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScreenConfig.mode` | `'create'` — `screen-nodes.ts:199` builds the ScreenSpec with `mode: cfg.mode === 'edit' ? 'edit' : 'create'` | `.default('create')` |
| `HttpConfig.method` | **two values** — `http-nodes.ts:218` inline `cfg.method ?? 'GET'`, `:168` durable `cfg.method ?? 'POST'` | ⛔ none |

Declaring `.default('GET')` on `method` would materialise `GET` at parse time, the durable arm's own `?? 'POST'` would never fire again, and every stored durable callout that omits the method would silently change verb — the defect this card exists to end, pointed the other way. That asymmetry is recorded in both files so the next reader does not "finish the job".

## Migration and declaration

- ADR-0087 **D3 semantic** entry `wait-node-event-config-required` under step 18 — a stored block-less `wait` node has no lossless conversion, because the missing value is an intent no artifact records, so the entry is a structured TODO naming each node to edit (`os migrate meta --from 17`). Registered by regeneration: `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` carries a GENERATED block and `check:migration-registry` reconciles it against `src/migrations/entries/`.
- Changeset: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation` with a **BREAKING** banner and its FROM → TO mapping — `minor` because the launch-window convention ships breaking changes as `minor` (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`), never `major`.
- `Clause-②: no`, and it was re-measured rather than inherited: `check-widening-tells --declaration no` over the whole diff exits **0 with zero tells**. `.default('create')` does not widen the accept set — a key that accepted absent/`undefined` still does; what moves is the OUTPUT type, which gets **narrower** (`'create' | 'edit'` where it was `'create' | 'edit' | undefined`). The declared-default plumbing it needs already existed (`authorable-defaults/automation.json` + `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR`), so this adds one entry to each rather than a mechanism.

## Verification

**Gates.** All **116** families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` from the actual 17-path change set were run, exit codes written to disk before any output was read, and reconciled with `--ran`: *116 derived, 116 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN*, every code `0`. Five needed a second pass and none of them was a red:

| family | first pass | why it was not a verdict | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` · `check:i18n` · `check:type-check-debt` | exit **3** | `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` — the gate reads built output and the repo was not fully built | all `0` after `turbo run build` over every workspace package (72/72 successful) |
| `check:skill-examples` | exit 1 | refused on `packages/client-react/dist` holding no declarations — a stated refusal to compute a verdict, not a finding | `0` |
| `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` | exit 1 | its positive control is pinned to a commit this shallow checkout could not reach; checker-health only, it cannot judge this diff | `0` after fetching that commit — 47 cases pass |

`check:type-check-debt` OOM'd on the second attempt too: the gate pins a CI-shaped 6144 MB ceiling and reports that the caller's `NODE_OPTIONS` is the tighter one. Raised to 8192 for that one command, on that stated reason; it then re-measured 5 ledger entries, 55 raw errors, none above its recorded number.

**Tests** (affected packages, plus the consumer package already in the diff):

| package | result |
| --- | --- |
| `@objectstack/spec` | 477 files / **13602** tests passed |
| `@objectstack/service-automation` | 135 files / **1599** tests passed |
| `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` | 45 files / **738** tests passed |
| typecheck, all three | pass, including each package's `check:test-typecheck` |

**Reverse verification of the cross-package type narrowing** — one-shot, both legs run from the committed state, the restore leg proven by blob hash rather than by an exit code:

```
HEAD blob             c9f88d74df30174720a85e1747e7a5ae5c1681ef
mutated blob          220adfac111a1b6e7229ad64a3e8292eb7810095   (probe really on disk)
MUTATED_TSC_EXIT=1    src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts(391,7): error TS2322:
                      Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type '"create" | "edit"'.
RESTORED_TSC_EXIT=0   git diff HEAD empty, blob back to c9f88d74
```

The probe was `ScreenConfigParsed["mode"] = undefined` in a consumer that imports the type. It compiles green against the OLD declaration and red against the new one, so the red proves `service-automation` resolved the **rebuilt** `packages/spec/dist/*.d.ts` and not a cached optional `mode`.

**The corpus parses.** `examples/app-showcase` builds its 30 flows through the narrowed contract with no edit, and a repo-wide sweep for `type: 'wait'` / `type: 'boundary_event'` in every spelling (TS, JSON, YAML, MDX) found no other fixture needing the block. The one that did — `plugin-approvals`' ADR-0044 revise-window flow — is in the diff, and its fixture now declares `{ eventType: 'signal', signalName: 'revision_submitted' }` so the send-back refusal it pins is measured against a flow that still registers.

## Acceptance notes

- ⭐ **A malformed or zero-valued `timerDuration` still reproduces the silent park** — out of scope for this PR, reported for triage to file. The contract can require the key but cannot evaluate the string: `parseIsoDuration` answers `undefined` for `'not-a-duration'`, for `'P'`, for `'PT0S'` and for `'0'` exactly as it did for the absent key, so no deadline is computed, no job is armed, no `waitUntil` is persisted, and the node still returns `{ success: true, suspend: true }`. The repro is live in the tree: `wait-node.test.ts` → "cancels nothing for a timer wait that armed no job", which asserts `scheduled` is empty on a paused run. It was left out deliberately — a format refinement narrows the accept set beyond what the ruling covers and adds a validation surface this card's gate families do not carry. A fixture comment on that branch previously claimed it was "Filed separately"; no card exists, and the comment is corrected in this PR rather than left asserting a filing nobody made.
- **In-place fix beyond this card, declared.** `parseEndNodeConfig`'s docblock in the same file carried the identical false clause — "Applied at the NODE level so an `end` nested in a region is checked exactly like a top-level one" — predating this branch (#14945). It is the same sentence, the same file, the same mechanism and the same published-to-npm surface, so leaving it would have shipped a file that contradicts itself two docblocks apart. Measured before correcting, not assumed: `FlowNodeSchema.safeParse` of a top-level `end` carrying `{ outcome: 'refused' }` and no `message` answers `false`; the identical node nested in a `loop` body passes `FlowSchema.safeParse` (`true`) and is refused only by `LoopConfigSchema`, at `body.nodes.0.config.message`. The clause is removed and cross-referenced to the one explanation so the two cannot drift. Prose only — no behaviour change, and `end` config handling is untouched.
- The four non-timer `eventType`s still carry no required resumer key of their own — `{ eventType: 'signal' }` with no `signalName` parses, and the executor correlates on `undefined`. Noted, not filed: no separate carrier, and it is the same shape as the row above rather than a second one.
